findings.message: The plan comprehensively addresses all requirements for a cross-roadmap readiness resolver with deterministic, checkpoint-aware resolution.

Plan correctly specifies exactly one '_get_ready_items' definition in roadmap-runtime that both autopilot-roadmap and the new resolver will import without module-name collisions. Current implementation shows this is achievable through proper sys.path management.

Plan correctly ensures checkpoint terminal sets remain authoritative when roadmap item status briefly diverges, without using advisory learnings, handoffs, queue state, mtimes, or time. This aligns with existing state-artifacts.md guidance.
Plan properly handles typed cross-roadmap dependencies through effective completion from checkpoint terminal sets and fails closed on malformed or identity-mismatched checkpoints as required.

Plan correctly defines implementable, deterministic semantics for source_fingerprint, stale flag, and diagnostics including missing checkpoints and unchanged-input byte identity through SHA-256 content hashing.
Plan properly defines the global (priority, roadmap_id, item_id) ordering and supervisor grouped compatibility projection as fully testable through deterministic output and schema validation.

Plan maintains coherent contract schema, tasks, package scope, lock set, dependency commit, validation commands, and single sequential package as evidenced by well-defined work-packages.yaml and comprehensive testing approach.
Plan correctly identifies no required schema migration, runtime mirror, documentation, security, deployment, or rollback work is omitted. The change is additive and preserves existing behavior.

Plan correctly ensures no breaking behavior is introduced - existing autopilot-roadmap call sites retain function signature and supervisor command retains grouped compatibility shape while consuming canonical result.
